title: The wrong part that became the pacemaker
hook: A wrong part pulled from a box ended up saving hearts.
summary: In 1956 engineer Wilson Greatbatch grabbed the wrong resistor, and his circuit pulsed like a heartbeat, leading to the implantable pacemaker.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Wikipedia, Wilson Greatbatch: in 1956 he installed a wrong-size resistor in a heart rhythm recorder, and the circuit produced intermittent pulses like a heartbeat.
National Inventors Hall of Fame / Smithsonian: Greatbatch worked in a barn workshop, and in 1960 his pacemaker was implanted in a 77-year-old man who lived about 18 more months.

lines.text: A wrong part pulled from a box ended up saving hearts.
In nineteen fifty-six, engineer Wilson Greatbatch was building a device to record heartbeats.
He reached for a resistor, but grabbed the wrong one.
lines.caps: He reached for a *resistor, | grabbed the *wrong one

lines.text: The circuit began to pulse, pause, and pulse again.
It sounded just like a heartbeat.
So he spent two years shrinking it in his barn.
In nineteen sixty, it went into a man of seventy-seven, who lived eighteen more months.
lines.caps: In *1960, | a man of *77 | lived *18 months

lines.text: One wrong part became the pacemaker.

post.caption:
A tiny mistake in a workshop now helps millions of hearts keep time.
Would you have noticed the mistake was a discovery?
